2607.25597.title: A Density-Matrix Framework for Electronic-Structure Analysis of Functional-Group and Salt Effects in Lithium-Metal Electrolytes
2607.25597.paper_summary: The reactivity of lithium-metal electrolytes arises from the interplay of molecular functional groups, Li$^+$ solvation, and salt-anion participation. This interplay operates through the redistribution of electron density across donor, anion, and cation centers, which is most directly read out from the electronic structure resolved in space. Quantum-chemical calculations deliver such readouts faithfully, yet become computationally demanding across this multidimensional design space, and machine-learning electronic-structure models seldom cover chemically diverse solvation shells or electrolyte-relevant readouts. Here, we present a density-matrix-centered AI platform (EMolStudio) for electronic-structure prediction and analysis. Its workflow integrates molecular functionalization, explicit Li$^+$ first-shell assembly, density-matrix prediction with idempotency projection, and readouts of frontier orbitals, electrostatic potential, Li$^+$-donor bond order, and electron localization. We apply EMolStudio to 163,655 functionalized molecules and 22,500 explicit Li$^+$ first-shell clusters across four lithium salts. We find that 1) at the molecular scale, functionalization distinguishes CO$_2$Me, CN, F/CF$_3$, and sulfonyl groups by chemically distinct changes in frontier levels, electrostatic potential, and Li$^+$-donor contact, consistent with $π^*$-acceptor, inductive, and polarization contributions, with sublinear accumulation at higher degrees of functionalization; 2) in explicit solvation shells, anion identity reshapes frontier-orbital localization: LiTDI anchors the HOMO on the anion across the entire library, whereas LiDFOB pairs an anion-hosted HOMO with strongly functional-group-dependent LUMO hosting. EMolStudio thereby translates functional-group and salt choices into electronic-structure hypotheses relevant to lithium-bond formation, desolvation, and interphase reactions.
2607.25597.paper_summary_zh: 鋰金屬電解質的反應性源於分子官能團、Li$^+$ 溶劑化和鹽陰離子參與之間的相互作用。這種相互作用通過在供體、陰離子和陽離子中心之間重新分配電子密度來運作，這在空間中最直接地從電子結構中讀出。量子化學計算能夠忠實地提供這些讀數，但在這個多維設計空間中變得計算上要求高，機器學習電子結構模型很少涵蓋化學多樣的溶劑殼或電解質相關的讀數。在這裡，我們提出了一個以密度矩陣為中心的人工智慧平台（EMolStudio）用於電子結構的預測和分析。其工作流程整合了分子官能化、明確的 Li$^+$ 第一層組裝、帶有冪等性投影的密度矩陣預測，以及前沿軌道、靜電勢、Li$^+$-供體鍵序和電子定位的讀數。我們將 EMolStudio 應用於 163,655 個功能化分子和 22,500 個明確的 Li$^+$ 第一層簇，涵蓋四種鋰鹽。我們發現 1) 在分子尺度上，功能化通過前沿能級、靜電勢和 Li$^+$-供體接觸的化學不同變化來區分 CO$_2$Me、CN、F/CF$_3$ 和磺酰基，這與 $π^*$-受體、感應和極化貢獻一致，且在更高的功能化程度下呈亞線性累積；2) 在明確的溶劑殼中，陰離子的身份重塑了前沿軌道的定位：LiTDI 在整個庫中將 HOMO 鎖定在陰離子上，而 LiDFOB 將一個陰離子主導的 HOMO 與強烈依賴官能團的 LUMO 主導配對。因此，EMolStudio 將官能團和鹽的選擇轉化為與鋰鍵形成、去溶劑化和界面反應相關的電子結構假設。
